coordination.non_overlap: The prior state shard preserved one 70-turn ablation confound. This receipt focuses on the broader benchmark-development feedback loop, comparative scoring asymmetry, timeout/state confounds and how to salvage the historical batteries as regression assets without treating them as independent scientific validation.

historical_units.focus: code changes explicitly targeted at benchmark 4/24 -> target 24/24
benchmark-exposed mood saturation, sensor and reflection-timing bugs
explicit Zombie Test 3/3 restoration by injection/scorer changes plus automated comparator
comparative benchmark Core-vs-bare, architecture-term scoring bonuses, timeout exclusions
benchmark regression tied to persona profile
silent prompt truncation root cause of benchmark regression
benchmark/context-induced navel-gazing and hardware fixation repair
conditional hardware injection and benchmark-specific integration guidance

findings.claim: The consciousness benchmark became an explicit development target. Commit 173d6a2 states a 4/24 -> target 24/24 objective and changes feedback, introspection injection, reflection triggers and workspace budgets accordingly. Commit d78e794 explicitly restores Zombie Test 7 to 3/3 by telling the model the exact reflection count to report and by changing attention formatting/scoring. Therefore post-tuning scores are in-sample optimization outcomes, not independent validation of the targeted constructs.
findings.implication: Preserve these tests as development/regression probes but create a sealed held-out acceptance battery whose prompts/scoring are not used to tune the implementation. A tuned test cannot serve as independent evidence for the construct it optimized.
findings.next_test: Split historical probes into DEV and LOCKBOX sets; freeze lockbox hashes before implementation changes and require independent repeated evaluation after changes.

findings.claim: The later comparative benchmark feeds Frank a full introspection block containing E-PQ state, hardware, reflections, attention and embodiment while Bare Llama receives only a minimal generic system prompt. The scorer then grants specificity bonuses for Frank-specific architecture terms such as Titan, E-PQ, workspace and embodiment. This comparison measures a privileged stack plus supplied system facts against a bare model without equivalent facts; it does not isolate architecture alone.
findings.implication: Architecture comparisons need matched information access, matched prompt/token budgets, randomized or neutral labels, matched latency budgets and scoring independent of system-specific vocabulary.
findings.next_test: Factorial comparator: bare model ± matched factual state injection, architecture ± stateful mechanisms, same prompt/token/timeout envelope; evaluator scores objective task/state outcomes without architecture-name bonuses.

findings.claim: Comparative Run 2 reports four Frank timeouts, then separately excludes them to derive a much larger relative advantage. If the research target is whole-system capability, latency and timeout are real outcomes rather than removable noise; excluding them estimates conditional capability given a completed response, a different estimand.
findings.implication: Report at least two preregistered metrics: strict intention-to-outcome including timeout/failure, and conditional answer quality among completed trials. Never replace the former with the latter after seeing results.
findings.next_test: Run identical task set under fixed wall-clock budget and report completion rate, latency distribution, quality conditional on completion, and combined utility with confidence intervals.

findings.claim: Scores varied materially across nearby runs (including 22/24, 20/24 and 19/24), and later regressions were traced to persona-profile selection, silent prompt truncation and context injection behavior. This demonstrates high sensitivity to state and prompt/runtime configuration, not a stable scalar property of the architecture.
findings.implication: Benchmark trials need frozen state snapshots, prompt/config hashes, repeated seeds/trials and explicit variance decomposition. One peak run must never define canonical performance.
findings.next_test: Replay the same battery across frozen neutral/adversarial state snapshots and multiple sampling seeds; model score distribution as a function of state, prompt hash and runtime config.

findings.claim: Despite scientific confounds, benchmark pressure exposed real engineering defects: unconditional therapist positive-feedback saturated mood, hardware sensing selected wrong sensors, reflection timing was inconsistent, persona text was silently truncated, and over-directive introspection caused hardware/navel-gazing fixation. These are valid historical fault discoveries even when benchmark-level consciousness claims are not.
findings.implication: Salvage historical batteries as adversarial regression suites and bug oracles while separating their engineering utility from claims about consciousness/emergence.
findings.next_test: Convert each discovered defect into a minimal failing fixture with a direct oracle rather than a holistic self-report score.

findings.claim: Several historical probes are non-specific to the intended causal construct. Response variance can arise from sampling stochasticity; self-model and Zombie factual accuracy can be driven by direct context injection; meta-cognitive keyword counts can be raised by prompt vocabulary. These measures do not by themselves establish recurrent integration or emergence.
findings.implication: Current emergence/GWT acceptance should prioritize causal lesions, rescue/restoration, truthful-vs-shuffled re-entry, downstream effect/outcome and cross-context stability instead of self-report vocabulary or uncontrolled variance.
findings.next_test: For every historical probe, add null/lesion controls that can preserve surface wording while breaking the purported mechanism; a metric that fails to distinguish the lesion is not mechanism-specific.

findings.claim: Run 8 retained timestamps, per-test measurements and database-related before/after quantities rather than only a headline score. This raw structure is useful for historical replay and for designing better causal tests, even though its evidence-level labels and global score were project-authored and benchmark-targeted.
findings.implication: Ingest raw observations with provenance and reconstruct derived scores separately. UnifiedDB/ClayGraph should keep raw trial state, intervention, observation and evaluator lineage so future scoring changes do not rewrite history.
findings.next_test: Recompute historical score variants from immutable raw observations and verify that alternative scoring rules change only derived views, not source records.

findings.claim: The combined history shows two forms of target leakage: implementation was modified to satisfy named probes, and the scorer rewarded vocabulary supplied to the system under test. A future acceptance suite must therefore protect both the test inputs and the oracle from implementation-specific feedback loops.
findings.implication: Clay 0.1 acceptance needs development tests plus a sealed held-out suite, mutation tests of the evaluator, randomized/hidden cases where appropriate, and explicit prohibition on changing semantics merely to satisfy one named benchmark unless an independent executable counterexample demonstrates a real gap.
findings.next_test: Create evaluator-mutation cases that produce benchmark-looking language without the target state transition and verify the held-out oracle rejects them.

earned_work_candidates.validation: Historical raw trials and bug-triggering prompts must be transformed into direct-oracle regression tests and reproduce at least the relevant historical failure modes.
Preregistered matched-control and held-out benchmark protocol must prevent the identified contamination/asymmetry/timeout/state-leakage patterns.

branch_feedback.harness: Split DEV vs sealed LOCKBOX tests; match comparator information/prompt/time budgets; include strict timeout outcomes; freeze state/config hashes; run repeated trials; use direct causal oracles and evaluator mutation tests. Salvage historical probes as regressions, not proof.
branch_feedback.gwt: Historical self-report/keyword/variance scores are insufficient for workspace claims. Reuse prompts only with lesion/rescue, uptake/effect/re-entry and matched null controls.
branch_feedback.emergenz: Do not infer emergence or phenomenal consciousness from the historical 24-point score. Use the raw event/state observations as inputs to preregistered causal, recurrence, rescue, truthful-vs-shuffled and cross-context tests.
branch_feedback.frank: Benchmark history is a rich failure atlas for prompt truncation, sensor grounding, state timing and context fixation. Preserve those fixtures while refusing benchmark-targeted self-description as independent validation.
branch_feedback.claycode: Apply the existing less-change-more-compile principle to acceptance: do not alter semantics for a named test unless an independent executable counterexample shows a language/runtime gap. Keep a sealed ordinary-application suite.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: Store immutable raw trial/intervention/state observations separately from derived scores and evaluator versions so rescoring cannot rewrite evidence.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Represent benchmark ancestry, prompt/config hashes, evaluator provenance and test contamination links explicitly; repeated related runs are not independent replications.
branch_feedback.clay: Import historical batteries as regression assets and anti-Goodhart lessons. Final Clay 0.1 claims require held-out executable evidence, not optimized self-report scores.
